title: The Afternoon Brief: Midday update: Gaza accord fractures, ferry toll climbs, Iran denies talks
dek: The day's picture has sharpened since morning: a disarmament agreement between Israel and Hamas is under severe strain as strikes continue, the Indonesian ferry death toll has risen, and a fundamental disagreement between Washington and Tehran over whether negotiations exist threatens to unravel the announced pause in military action.
author: GoCheckMyNews
key_fact: Three separate crises now show the same fracture: announced frameworks (Gaza disarmament, US-Iran talks, WestJet labor peace) exist on paper but lack mutual acknowledgment or compliance from at least one party, leaving each accord's durability in question.
bottom_line: Three separate frameworks announced or reached Friday through Sunday, the Gaza disarmament roadmap, US-Iran negotiations, and the WestJet labor tentative deal, all show the same fracture: at least one party denies the accord's reality, rejects its terms, or has not yet ratified it. The day's theme is the gap between announced resolution and actual compliance. Watch for union ratification of the WestJet deal, any clarification from Iran or the US on whether talks are underway, Israeli conduct regarding the Gaza roadmap, and updated casualty counts from the Indonesian ferry and the Idaho shooting investigation's findings on motive.
body: The day has deepened three fault lines beneath what appeared to be diplomatic progress or resolution. In Gaza, the disarmament roadmap announced Friday requires Israel to withdraw troops and Hamas to surrender weapons in tandem, yet Israeli military aircraft continued strikes across Gaza City, Khan Younis, and Deir el-Balah for a second successive night, killing at least 13 people according to Palestinian officials. Trump called the agreement a "big step for the Middle East" on Friday; Israeli officials have publicly expressed skepticism about its viability. The framework exists; the parties do not.

The Iran-US disagreement is starker still. Trump announced Sunday that negotiations would begin Monday afternoon after calling off what he described as massive military strikes. Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei stated Monday: "We currently do not have negotiations with America." Trump said the deal would include "the Hormuz Strait and also, ultimately, the denuclearization of Iran" and that Iran faces no deadline. The two governments are not even agreeing on whether they are talking.

The WestJet tentative agreement, by contrast, is a resolution in form but not yet in fact. The airline and flight attendant union CUPE 8125 reached a tentative deal ending a strike that cancelled 495 flights and affected 250,000 travelers. The accord addresses the core dispute: compensation for ground-based work flight attendants perform before departure. But the deal still requires union ratification, and the specific terms of how that work will be paid remain undisclosed.

Other developments: the Indonesian ferry KMP Mutiara Sentosa 2, which caught fire off Madura island early Saturday with at least 250 people aboard, now has five confirmed dead and 41 still missing. The fire began around 06:00 to 07:00 local time but was not reported to Indonesia's National Search and Rescue Agency until 08:24, a delay of roughly two to two-and-a-half hours. The cause remains unknown. In Idaho, three people were killed and five injured in a shooting outside an In-N-Out Burger in Twin Falls on Saturday at 2:29 p.m.; the suspected shooter is also dead. Police said there is no longer a threat to the community, but investigators continue to establish the shooter's identity and motive. In a separate development, JPMorgan Chase announced a $750 billion housing investment through 2035, including financing for 1 million affordable units and assistance for 500,000 homebuyers, a 40 percent increase in the bank's housing capital compared to the prior decade. Finally, the US Treasury and Japan's Ministry of Finance jointly intervened in currency markets Friday to halt the yen's decline to a 40-year low, the first coordinated intervention between the two countries since 2011.

The honest read is that announced frameworks and tentative agreements are proliferating while actual compliance and mutual commitment remain in question. Gaza has a disarmament roadmap but no ceasefire holding it. Washington and Tehran have announced talks but cannot agree they are happening. WestJet's tentative deal halts disruption but leaves the central question unresolved until members vote.
